subject: Urgent — H2 compression-profile swap caused tail latency and accuracy regressions
messages:
From: Asha Patel <asha@latticehealth.com>
To: olga_petrov <olga@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Cc: tom.greene <tom.greene@latticehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 14:07:00 -0800
Subject: Sudden p95/tail latency and accuracy drift after tonight's H2 compression swap

Hi Olga / Lauren,

We rolled traffic onto the model you upgraded last night (Redwood model v2.2 alpha with compression-profile H2). Since ~02:30 UTC we are seeing a step increase in tail latency and a rise in semantic misclassification on our clinical triage classifier. Quick numbers from our monitoring: p95 latency jumped from ~750ms to ~1.2s, error rate (mislabels) from 0.35% to ~1.6%, and sustained throughput dropped ~18% at peak.

Our users are seeing delayed responses and a handful of clinically relevant misclassifications — I attached a small sample (semantic-drift-examples.txt) and a tail latency CSV. This is customer-impacting. Can you confirm whether Redwood applied the H2 compression-profile swap for our dedicated fleet at ~02:10 UTC and advise next steps? We need either an immediate rollback or an urgent mitigation.

Asha
Director, AI Platform
LatticeHealth

From: olga_petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Cc: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Sudden p95/tail latency and accuracy drift after tonight's H2 compression swap

Folks — forwarding an urgent customer escalation from LatticeHealth (DEAL-4982). They report tail latency and semantic drift after the H2 compression-profile swap that went live during our maintenance window.

Summary:
- Affected: dedicated deployment for LatticeHealth (us-west region).
- Symptom: p95 up ~+450ms, error/mislabeling up ~1.25pp, throughput down ~18%.
- Timeline: profile swap completed ~2027-03-03T02:10:00Z per rollout logs.

Attachments: request_logs.tar.gz (they included logs), tail_latency-sample.csv, semantic-drift-examples.txt.

Immediate asks:
1) Can infra confirm the exact kernel/quant profile used and whether fallback variants were served?
2) Product/infra: propose fast mitigation (rollback to H1 or scale-up) and estimate time-to-remediate (ETA).
3) Account: advise on communications and whether we need to offer credits up-front.

Please treat as P1 and reply with concrete actions. I can join a 15:00 UTC call if needed.

—Olga
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

From: lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
To: olga_petrov <olga@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Cc: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 15:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden p95/tail latency and accuracy drift after tonight's H2 compression swap

Thanks Olga — looping in a few clarifying asks:

1) Confirm the model binary and quant path: which quantization profile file was applied (profile id and checksum)? Was this a full-traffic flip or a staggered canary?
2) Any change to kernel selection or custom fused ops for this profile?
3) Are cached KV prefixes invalidated by this profile change (could explain throughput drop)?

Short-term mitigation I recommend: start a controlled rollback to compression-profile H1 for the LatticeHealth pool only (canary -> 50% -> 100%), but hold if rollback risks producing other regressions. Marcus, can infra create an isolated plan to revert H2 for only the dedicated GPU pool and stand up extra nodes if we need to absorb load?

If the rollback is low-risk we should execute immediately (target <90 minutes). If not, scale up nodes to reduce queueing while we investigate.

-Lauren
Director, Product (Inference)

From: marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, olga_petrov <olga@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 15:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden p95/tail latency and accuracy drift after tonight's H2 compression swap

Quick infra assessment:
- Rollout logs show the H2 profile was enabled cluster-wide for LatticeHealth pool at 2027-03-03T02:12:04Z. Profile checksum: a3f9b2d. Kernel probe selected AVX-mixed-fused path on host group us-west-2-gpuA.
- Observed queueing on hot-shard nodes consistent with higher model CPU-prep time under H2. That explains throughput dip and tail.

Mitigation options (ranked):
1) Immediate targeted rollback to profile H1 for the LatticeHealth pool (low-risk). ETA ~45 minutes if we have approval to run the revert and accept transient request re-routing. Will require a short maintenance window and potential cold-starts for a subset of pods.
2) Temporarily scale pool capacity by +25% to drain queues while we validate H2 behavior. ETA ~20 minutes to spin up; cost impact is material but reversible.
3) Apply runtime patch to force legacy kernel selection for H2 (short-term hack) — ETA ~90 minutes, riskier.

We have Jira ticket H2SWAP-987 tracking the rollback. Need Rishi/Stef approval for option 1 (customer rollback) because it's a prod change touching an enterprise allocation and has SLA/comp implications.

-Marcus
Head of Platform Reliability

From: Asha Patel <asha@latticehealth.com>
To: olga_petrov <olga@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Cc: tom.greene <tom.greene@latticehealth.com>, procurement@latticehealth.com
Date: Thu, 4 Mar 2027 02:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Sudden p95/tail latency and accuracy drift after tonight's H2 compression swap

Thanks for the quick triage. Attaching a few more examples (semantic-drift-examples.txt) — our QA flagged clinically significant mislabels for "respiratory distress" vs "non-urgent cough" that would change triage priority. We are pausing a portion of traffic and can divert to a safe-mode route, but that reduces our throughput and user experience.

We appreciate a rollback if it will restore behaviour. Also want to flag we may request remediation credits if SLA is breached — please loop account exec for compensation discussion. ETA here is quite urgent — our ops team needs a remediation ETA within the hour or we escalate to our CISO.

Asha

From: olga_petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Cc: Asha Patel <asha@latticehealth.com>, Tom Greene <tom.greene@latticehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Mar 2027 15:02:00 +0000
Subject: Exec escalation: approval needed to rollback H2 for LatticeHealth + proposed customer remediation

Team — escalation to execs. LatticeHealth (DEAL-4982) is P1 impacted; their production classification errors have clinical implications. Marcus recommends Option 1 (targeted rollback to H1 for their dedicated pool).

Requested approvals:
- Rishi: approve immediate targeted rollback to H1 for the LatticeHealth pool (ETA ~45 min). This is a prod change but the customer is asking for a revert to restore correctness.
- Stephanie: approve an up-front goodwill credit for any SLA impact (recommendation: 20% of March committed usage or equivalent service credit) and authorize outreach from account team.

I've attached an exec one-pager summarizing impact, timeline, and recommended language for customer communication (exec-one-pager.pdf). If you approve, Marcus will execute rollback and Lauren will coordinate checks and post-rollback validation.

If no immediate approval, we will scale capacity (+25%) as a stopgap. I propose a 15:00 UTC call to sign off.

—Olga
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
